verified_scholarly_sources.title: Detecting Targeted Attacks Using Shadow Honeypots
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: High false positive rates in anomaly detection causing service disruption, and isolated honeypots failing to protect live production traffic.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Inline anomaly detector monitors production traffic; suspicious requests are diverted to instrumented shadow honeypots mirroring application state; verified attacks are safely aborted while false alarms are processed and transparently returned.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Prototype evaluated on Apache web server and Mozilla Firefox client under simulated buffer overflows and web exploits.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Foundational architectural ancestor: selective inline diversion of suspicious requests to an isolated deceptive replica based on anomaly detection.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Shadow honeypots require full memory/internal application state mirroring and rollbacks to service false positives; this project routes traffic to independent synthetic services with a Deception State Graph and explicitly treats uncontained observe-only attacks as origin leakage.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Anomaly Detection of Web-based Attacks
verified_scholarly_sources.venue: 10th ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '03)
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Detecting novel web application attacks without pre-existing signature definitions.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Multi-model statistical anomaly detection on HTTP requests: attribute length, character distribution (entropy), structural token order, and parameter presence.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Empirical evaluation on DARPA 1999 dataset and live departmental web server traffic.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Direct overlap with feature extraction methodology: request length, Shannon entropy, special character ratios, and keyword tokens.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Kruegel & Vigna relied on statistical distribution heuristics; this project integrates supervised random forest inference with a deterministic regex bypass and dynamic routing policy.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: A Game-Theoretic Taxonomy and Survey of Defensive Deception for Cybersecurity and Privacy
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Lack of unified theoretical models to categorize and optimize defensive deception across diverse network layers.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Formal taxonomy classifying defensive deception games: incomplete information games, signaling games, hypergames, and stochastic Markov games.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Taxonomic literature analysis and theoretical formalization of deception trade-offs and belief manipulation.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Theoretical foundation for modeling adversary belief states and progressive interaction phases.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Pawlick et al. emphasize mathematical equilibrium concepts (Nash, Stackelberg, PBNE); this project implements a practical finite state graph (DSG) with deterministic policy bounds rather than dynamic equilibrium solving.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Examining the Efficacy of Decoy-based and Psychological Cyber Deception
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Absence of empirical, human-subject evidence validating whether cyber deception actually degrades attacker efficacy.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Controlled red-team experimentation (The Tularosa Study) measuring attacker time allocation, dwell time on decoys, and tactical task disruption.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Empirical study with 130+ professional red teamers across multi-day network penetration exercises.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Direct conceptual foundation for the Deception Effectiveness Score (DES) dwell time ($T_{\text{dwell}}$) and decoy interaction ($E_{\text{engagement}}$) components.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Ferguson-Walter et al. evaluated human cognitive confusion and psychological framing across subnets; this project models synthetic API request interactions and mathematical metric gates in a reverse proxy.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Deception Techniques in Computer Security: A Research Perspective
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Fragmented deception techniques and lack of architectural principles for maintaining realistic deception.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Systematic survey of honeypots, honeytokens, network decoys, and deception orchestration; emphasizes the critical role of environment consistency to prevent fingerprinting.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Taxonomic survey and comparative analysis across operating systems, networks, and applications.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Highlights the necessity of cross-service state consistency and session coherence to prevent honeypot discovery.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Han et al. survey broad system-level decoys; this project provides an architectural implementation restricted to L7 HTTP reverse proxying, session stickiness, and allowlisted synthetic data.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Toward Proactive, Adaptive Defense: A Survey on Moving Target Defense
verified_scholarly_sources.thematic_area: Moving Target Defense & Dynamic Surface Mutation
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Static network defenses give asymmetric advantages to persistent attackers who can conduct reconnaissance indefinitely.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Taxonomy of MTD techniques: IP shuffling, runtime binary mutation, dynamic routing, and decoy instantiation.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Systematic literature survey and trade-off analysis between security gains and system performance overhead.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Conceptual alignment on dynamic surface switching and adaptive routing away from static production endpoints.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: MTD alters the actual operational surface; this project maintains a static origin behind a reverse proxy and selectively diverts malicious sessions to deceptive mock services.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: A Survey of Moving Target Defenses for Network Security
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Asymmetric information advantages in network reconnaissance and targeted lateral movement.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Survey of network-layer MTD, software-defined network (SDN) dynamic flow steering, and attack graph modeling.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Survey of quantitative evaluation frameworks, game-theoretic formulations, and testbed implementations.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Examines dynamic routing and diversion of network flows as defensive measures.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Sengupta et al. focus heavily on SDN OpenFlow rule mutations at L3/L4; this project operates strictly at L7 (HTTP reverse proxy) using application-layer session cookies and headers.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: An anomaly-based approach for intrusion detection in web traffic
verified_scholarly_sources.venue: Journal of Information Assurance and Security
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Evaluating web intrusion detection algorithms on structured HTTP transactions with e-commerce parameters.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Generated the CSIC 2010 dataset against experimental web app 'tienda1' using web crawlers and automated scanners (Paros, Nessus).
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Clustering and statistical anomaly scoring on HTTP request payloads.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Primary dataset source for Stage 11 external benchmark (69/100 scenarios).
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Torrano-Giménez et al. used the dataset for offline anomaly model benchmarking; this project incorporates it into an active gateway routing and session deception evaluation framework.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Honware: A Virtual Honeypot Framework for Capturing CPE and IoT Zero Days
verified_scholarly_sources.venue: 2019 APWG Symposium on Electronic Crime Research (eCrime)
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: Scalable emulation of diverse web-facing firmware and web applications without manual honeypot authoring.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Automated firmware unpacking and virtual emulation to stand up responsive web interfaces for capturing real-world exploits.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Empirical deployment capturing large-scale Internet worm and botnet propagation.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Addresses stateful emulation of web applications for threat capture.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Honware emulates complete firmware images for broad Internet-facing scanning; this project provides a modular reverse proxy that selectively diverts traffic from an enterprise origin to containerized synthetic mocks.

verified_scholarly_sources.title: Using Generalization and Characterization to Detect Web-Based Attacks
verified_scholarly_sources.venue: 13th Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS 2006)
verified_scholarly_sources.thematic_area: Anomaly Generalization & False Positive Reduction in Web IDS
verified_scholarly_sources.problem_addressed: High false alarm rates in web anomaly detection due to benign variation in application parameters.
verified_scholarly_sources.technical_mechanism: Techniques to generalize anomaly rules across parameters and characterize anomalies using structural signatures to discard benign noise.
verified_scholarly_sources.evaluation_method: Evaluation on operational university web servers processing millions of requests.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_overlap: Addresses the identical challenge observed in Stage 10/11: distinguishing benign parameter variations from true attacks.
verified_scholarly_sources.project_distinction: Robertson et al. tuned anomaly models to suppress false alarms; this project introduces an intermediate 'OBSERVE_ONLY' policy routing state that balances risk by passing ambiguous requests to origin while escalating observation.

verified_patent_documents.title: Network intrusion diversion using a software defined network
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A method comprising receiving network packets directed to a physical computer on an enterprise network; determining an intrusion attempt; utilizing an SDN controller to divert packets from the physical computer to a decoy software-based host emulator having the exact same IP address as the physical computer.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Core functional concept of identifying an intrusion attempt and dynamically diverting traffic from a legitimate target to a decoy emulation environment.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 10,193,924 operates at the SDN network packet layer using OpenFlow flow modifications and IP address duplication. This project operates at Layer 7 (HTTP reverse proxy) using application-layer session cookies, ML score thresholds, and finite state graph (DSG) mock APIs.

verified_patent_documents.title: Tunneling for network deceptions
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A system comprising a network device on a first network configured as a projection point for a network tunnel terminating at a deception center on a second network; assigning an IP address from the first network to a deception mechanism in the deception center to project decoys into the first network.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Separation of primary enterprise network from an isolated deception runtime environment.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 9,979,750 claims network-layer GRE/IPsec tunneling and subnet IP assignment to project decoys into local broadcast domains. This project uses an application-layer reverse proxy forwarding HTTP requests over Docker bridge networks to an unexposed container.

verified_patent_documents.title: Responsive deception mechanisms
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A method of deploying low-interaction decoys; detecting initial attacker interaction; dynamically promoting or escalating the low-interaction decoy into a high-interaction decoy to capture detailed adversary behavior.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Progressive escalation of deception detail based on attacker interaction stages.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 10,348,763 escalates physical/virtual machine honeypot interaction levels (low to high VM). This project modulates response detail and synthetic delay across finite states (RECON -> DISCOVERY -> EXPLOITATION -> CREDENTIAL_ACCESS) within a single containerized Node.js service.

verified_patent_documents.title: Luring attackers towards deception servers
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A system establishing payload-free connections between endpoints and a deception server to populate local connection caches; acquiring IP addresses across multiple VLANs; and using broadcast traffic to lure attackers toward deception servers.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Luring attackers away from production assets to deceptive environments.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 10,375,110 lures attackers via endpoint breadcrumbs, ARP/VLAN cache poisoning, and fake broadcast traffic. This project is strictly an in-line ingress HTTP gateway that evaluates incoming web requests and executes policy-driven diversion.

verified_patent_documents.title: Deceiving an attacker who is present in a computer network
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A method comprising deploying deceptive credentials and deceptive connection artifacts onto endpoint computers; monitoring usage of deceptive credentials to detect attackers attempting lateral movement.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Use of deceptive identity tokens to trap adversaries.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 10,333,977 focuses on endpoint memory/disk credential planting (Active Directory tokens, cached SSH keys). This project operates at the web API layer using synthetic HTTP authentication endpoints (`/api/auth/login`) and synthetic response schemas.

verified_patent_documents.title: Adaptive deception system
verified_patent_documents.assignee: The United States of America as represented by the Director, National Security Agency (NSA)
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: An adaptive deception system comprising an observation engine monitoring entity interaction with network nodes; a deception decision module dynamically modifying deception profiles based on observed threat scores; and an orchestration module reconfiguring decoys.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Dynamic modification of deception response profiles based on observed threat scoring and entity behavioral history.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 11,934,948 is an enterprise-wide node orchestration architecture. This project implements a lightweight edge gateway reverse proxy with a mathematically gated Deception Effectiveness Score (DES) and tenant-scoped application routing.

verified_patent_documents.title: Decoy and deceptive data object technology
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: A method of detecting cyber threats comprising monitoring interaction with decoy data objects placed in network shares; dynamically deploying deceptive operating systems and services upon detecting unauthorized operations.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Dynamic instantiation of deceptive services upon threat detection.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 2017/0134423 A1 relies on bait files and network share tripwires. This project intercepts live inbound HTTP traffic at the ingress gateway and diverts sessions to synthetic REST endpoints.

verified_patent_documents.title: Software Defined Networking Moving Target Defense Honeypot
verified_patent_documents.independent_claims_summary: Claim 1: An MTD honeypot system utilizing an SDN controller to dynamically reconfigure network flow routes, shifting IP/port mappings and directing anomalous flows into adaptive honeypots while preserving benign traffic routes.
verified_patent_documents.technical_overlap: Separation of anomalous flows from benign flows, directing the former to adaptive honeypots.
verified_patent_documents.technical_distinctions: US 11,876,833 requires an OpenFlow/SDN controller manipulating packet headers and switch flow tables. This project uses an application-layer reverse proxy with multi-tenant domain verification and session cookie routing.
